problems: The fire is not fire: in every frame it is a few flat, glowing pale-yellow planks with no flame, embers or smoke (board frames 1-14, at-50).
There is no sign of wind anywhere: no smoke drift, no flame lean, no grass or leaves moving, so 'steady wind', 'downwind' and 'upwind' cannot be read from the film.
The glowing planks jump in size and angle from frame to frame (board frames 1-7 grow into a long diagonal beam, frame 8 suddenly collapses) instead of burning.
The 'stake that catches, chars and falls' cannot be followed: a black stick appears lying on the ground by frame 8 with no fall seen, and it is not clear which stake it was.

At the end the whole fire vanishes between board frames 14 and 15 instead of dying down; the stakes in the foreground look unchanged, so 'the ones upwind stay standing' shows nothing happening to them.
Grass blades and a pink ring-shaped object sit inside the glowing planks (at-50), clipping through the fire; the foreground stakes cover part of the fire.
The yellow bird stands in the background in every frame, frozen and taking no part.
posts.critique: A viewer sees glowing yellow boards flickering behind some posts and then blinking out; neither the wind nor a stake catching and falling can be seen, so the caption claims a story the film does not show.

problems: Nobody spins the top or lowers the plate: no hand or creature acts, yet the caption says 'I spun' and 'lowered'; the plate just sinks by itself (board frames 1-6).
The glass plate sinks into the lodestone ring and disappears inside it (board frames 5-7) instead of being taken away: a clipping.
The top hangs perfectly still at one spot for the whole second half, with no wobble or visible spin (board frames 7-16, at-50), so 'spinning' is not visible and it reads as a frozen object floating.
The setup is plain shapes: a flat dark-grey polygon disc and a matte black ring on bare grass; the 'lodestone' looks like neither stone nor ore.
Half-seen creatures cut into the frame edges (a pink leg at top left, a grey leg at right in frames 9-15) and draw the eye away from the tiny top.
posts.critique: The plate melts into the ring with no one moving it, and the top then hangs motionless like a frozen model, so it reads as broken animation rather than a levitating spinning top.

problems: The 'magnet stone' is a plain black cube with no stone texture, lit flat and dull (board, at-75).
It barely moves in 4.4 s and turns slightly with no visible cause; nothing shows it gliding 'by itself' as a deliberate motion.
The 'thin iron spikes' are short brown sticks lying flat on the grass; they look like twigs, not standing iron spikes.
A spike pokes through the cube (board frames 11-16, at-75): a clipping.
The first frame is a dark fade; the whole film is washed out and hazy, with a huge shadow covering most of the ground and a grey-blue tree root cut off at the left edge.
posts.critique: A dark box nudging slightly among scattered twigs on a hazy, flat field: there is nothing to follow, the stone and spikes don't look like what the caption names, and the spike clips through the cube.

problems: The needle jumps to unrelated angles from one frame to the next (board frames 4-12) rather than swinging back and forth smoothly about one direction, so it reads as jitter, not a swing.
The whole film is covered by a grey-green haze; colors are washed out and the light is flat (board, at-50).
The 'bowl' is a plain grey polygon ring with a flat blue disc for water, and the 'lily pad' is a flat green ellipse with no shape; nothing looks like stone, water or a leaf.
The needle is a thin stick, small in the middle of the frame; the subject is tiny while a blurry flower bush fills the top left.
posts.critique: A flat, foggy disk with a small red stick that snaps between angles; it does not look like a compass bowl or a swinging needle, and it is not something to show anyone.
